title: Failure of disjoint additivity under magnetic Gauss constraints
abstract: Under local magnetic Gauss constraints, vertex-disjoint regions can have commuting physical observable algebras that do not generate all observables on their union. We construct such counterexamples for every finite non-Abelian group on regular square tori, retaining the full magnetic physical space and original supports inside a fixed contractible disk. A peripheral projector selects inputs on which a joint transition preserves the constraints, while its loop factor alone fails the universal test over physical exterior completions. For a specified support family around a fixed eight-edge square loop, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and each inner face is covered by at least one of its two prescribed peripheral edges. Leaving a face uncovered restores full additivity. For the same loop, additivity also holds with any region at vertex-set graph distance at least two. These results refute a recent group-double additivity proposition.
summary: This theoretical paper proves that for quantum systems on a torus with magnetic Gauss constraints, the algebra of observables on a union of disjoint regions does not necessarily equal the join of the individual algebras if the underlying symmetry group is non-Abelian. The failure is precisely characterized by the local geometry of the support regions relative to the magnetic constraints.
main_problem: The paper investigates the failure of 'disjoint additivity' for physical observable algebras in quantum systems subjected to local magnetic Gauss constraints.
main_result: Disjoint additivity fails for every finite non-Abelian group on a square torus lattice, unless specific geometric conditions (like leaving an inner face uncovered) are met.
method: The analysis uses the framework of magnetic double models, comparing the algebra generated by the union of two regions to the join of the individual algebras.
model_or_system: The system is defined on a regular square torus lattice and is governed by magnetic Gauss constraints involving a finite group G. The observables are studied via their $	ext{C}^*$-algebras.
key_observables: Physical observable algebras $A(R)$, joint transition operators $c_{WK}$, and loop factors $T_L$.
important_parameters: The structure of the finite group G (specifically, whether it is non-Abelian) and the geometric coverage of inner faces on the torus.
main_assumptions: The analysis retains the full magnetic physical space and original edge supports, avoiding electric or global-sector projections.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the failure and restoration of additivity for a fixed eight-edge loop on a square torus, showing strict inclusion when all faces are covered for non-Abelian groups.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mathematical machinery to test additivity, deriving conditions based on loop operators and joint observables, and concludes by proving the failure of additivity under specific group and geometric constraints.
why_interesting: The failure of simple additivity rules in constrained quantum systems is a deep topic relevant to understanding entanglement structure and locality in topological quantum field theories.
